classification_reason: Acceptance criteria require several unspecified design decisions: join-table/entity shape, global vs per-alert tag uniqueness, case-insensitive normalization strategy, and exact semantics of the 10-tag cap and delete-by-name lookup. Resolved via conservative assumptions below; implementation-plan.md and requirement-analysis.md record the decisions.
story_description: As an operator, I want to attach multiple free-form tags to an alert so I can filter alerts by tag.
acceptance_criteria: New Tag concept with a many-to-many relationship to Alert using a new join table/migration
POST /api/alerts/{id}/tags adds one or more tags, deduplicates case-insensitively, maximum 10 tags per alert, each tag 1-30 characters
DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} removes a tag and returns 404 if the alert or tag assignment does not exist
GET /api/alerts gains an optional tag query filter composable with isActive, severity, date range, and search
exact_source_files: AlertService.Data/Interfaces/IAlertRepository.cs (add tag filter param + tag mutation methods)
exact_source_files_note: Exceeds the default 5-file cap deliberately: the story spans a new domain concept (Tag), a new join table/migration, and touches every layer (Models -> Data -> Data.SQL -> DTO -> API) per repo-profile.md layering. This is the smallest file set that satisfies all five acceptance criteria.

design_decisions.tag_entity: Tag { Id (int PK), Name (string, 1-30 chars, trimmed) }. Tags are shared/global rows so the same word is never duplicated in the Tags table; case-insensitive lookup reuses an existing row.
design_decisions.join_entity: Explicit AlertTag { AlertId (FK), TagId (FK) } with composite PK (AlertId, TagId), matching the repo's existing explicit-configuration-class pattern (see AlertConfiguration.cs) instead of EF Core's implicit skip-navigation join table.
design_decisions.case_insensitive_dedup: Normalize incoming tag text by trimming; look up existing Tag rows using a case-insensitive comparison (string.Equals(..., StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) in the repository query, consistent with the existing search filter's ToLower() pattern in AlertRepository.GetAllAsync). SQL Server's default collation is already case-insensitive, so a unique index on Tag.Name enforces this at the DB level too.
design_decisions.max_10_tags_per_alert: Enforced in AlertManagementService before persisting: reject (400) the whole request if the resulting distinct tag count on the alert (existing + new, after case-insensitive de-dup) would exceed 10. Nothing is partially applied.
design_decisions.length_validation: Each submitted tag must be 1-30 characters after trimming; validated via DataAnnotations on AddAlertTagsRequest plus a defensive check in the service layer.
design_decisions.delete_semantics: DELETE /api/alerts/{id}/tags/{tag} matches {tag} case-insensitively against the alert's assigned tags; 404 if the alert does not exist OR the alert has no such tag assigned (acceptance criterion explicitly calls out both cases).
design_decisions.get_all_tag_filter: AlertQueryRequest gains an optional `Tag` string property; when present, AlertRepository.GetAllAsync filters alerts that have a Tag whose Name matches case-insensitively, composable (ANDed) with existing isActive/severity/date-range/search filters.
design_decisions.alert_response_shape: AlertResponse.Tags is IReadOnlyList<string> (tag names only) to avoid leaking internal Tag ids and keep the contract minimal, consistent with other response DTOs in AlertService.DTO/Responses.

out_of_scope: Authorization/roles for tag operations (none exist elsewhere in the service)
